platforms.heading: Platforms
platforms.intro: DM your Oru on Feishu / Discord, and it carries on with your work on the desktop. Generate a pairing code on the desktop and send it to the bot in a DM to bind — by default no one can use it; only once bound does it recognize you.
platforms.remoteDefaultDesc: Messages from Feishu / Discord all go to it (using its memory, projects, and approval gear)
platforms.pairingCodeDesc: Click to generate, then send it to the bot in a DM to bind (valid for a few minutes)
platforms.whitelistEmpty: No one bound yet — by default all remote messages are rejected; binding lets them through.
platforms.whitelistBound: Bound; removing requires the user to pair again
platforms.whitelistAddId: Paste a user ID to add manually

platforms.userAuthNotAuthorized: Not authorized — once authorized, Oru can read and write Feishu docs as you (docs belong to you)

usage.heading: Usage
usage.subtitle: Tokens spent on each model call, accounted by purpose. If one purpose costs a lot, switch it to a cheaper model under "Models".
usage.empty: No usage recorded for this period yet.
usage.tokenOnlyNote: Measured in tokens only — tokens are the settled fact of spend and never go stale; prices vary by provider, so no monetary estimate is shown here. Refer to your provider bill for actual charges.

budget.title: Usage budget
budget.enableDesc: Set two reminder lines on your last-30-days usage. Off by default — your budget is your call on your own wallet; it only applies once enabled.
budget.hardLimitDesc: When last-30-days usage reaches this, you get a more prominent reminder. For now it only reminds — it won't interrupt any task; stopping or adjusting the budget is your call.
budget.softRatioDesc: Sends a heads-up when you reach this fraction of the limit, so you can adjust before hitting the ceiling.

permissions.heading: Permissions
permissions.approvalDesc: Read-only = can only look and inspect, never act (writing files, editing files, commands that change things, installing MCP plugins, writing skills, committing to git, writing memory are all rejected outright; connected external tools are also disabled since their safety can't be judged — switch to “Work” to use them). Work = free to act, asking only on destructive actions like delete, overwrite, or system changes. Danger = fully free; only absolute catastrophes like rm -rf / or wiping a disk are still hard-blocked. This gear also governs the safety level of any subagent it dispatches.
permissions.approvalWork: Work · only asks on risky actions
permissions.presenceDesc: When on, hold ⌥ and click in any app and Oru comes over to chime in; requires granting “Input Monitoring” and “Screen Recording” in System Settings
permissions.keepAwakeDesc: When on, Oru keeps this Mac from sleeping and dimming the screen while it's running a turn or a background task; resumes normal sleep behavior when done. Off by default.
permissions.screenDenied: Not granted — needed to capture the screen area you ⌥-click
permissions.inputDesc: After granting, restart Oru to receive global ⌥-clicks from any app
permissions.loopMaxRoundsDesc: Max rounds a /loop task runs before stopping (1–20). Token budget is capped separately.

data.heading: Data
data.autoArchiveDesc: Long-inactive conversations move into “Archived” in the sidebar; sending a message brings them back to active
data.confirmArchiveDesc: When off, archiving moves the conversation straight into “Archived” without confirmation (it can still be restored; permanent deletion is done in “Archived”)
data.archiveHoursDesc: How many hours without a new message before auto-archiving
data.exportDesc: Pack all your data — memory, conversations, schedules — into one backup file you can carry to a new device
data.includeKeysDesc: Includes plaintext keys so a new machine needs no re-entry — but leaking the file leaks the keys. Off by default; re-enter once after restore
data.restoreDesc: Point at a backup file to restore. Overwrites all data on this device (auto safety-backup first), then restarts
data.clearMainConfirm:
Clear the main conversation?

The old chat history will be archived as a .jsonl.bak.<timestamp> file in {{name}}'s home folder,
but a fresh session will start on the SDK side ({{name}} won't remember the earlier conversation).

policy.intro: Whether each kind of action asks you first. On = run directly from now on; off = ask every time again. The defaults are the recommended balance — change them anytime.
policy.modifierZone: Special cases (these rules win when they apply)
policy.readonlyNote: Readonly mode: look but don’t touch — writes never run on their own. The policy table is only editable in Work mode.
policy.dangerNote: Danger mode: everything runs without asking except catastrophic actions. The policy table is only editable in Work mode.
policy.persistFailed: Couldn’t save the always-allow — this kind will be asked again after restart
policy.askPersistFailed: Couldn’t save the setting — this row returns to its default after restart
